sender_role: Fractional COO | Operations Consultant | Transformation Partner
sender_summary: Chris Ringenberg is an experienced Fractional COO and Operations Consultant who embeds with large franchise and real estate organizations to build scalable operational infrastructure. He specializes in franchise system operations, cross-functional process design, and leading transformation initiatives for complex, multi-unit organizations navigating competitive disruption. Chris works with senior leadership teams who have a clear strategic vision but need senior operational depth to execute it — building the systems, reporting frameworks, and organizational structures that convert strategy into consistent field-level performance.
receiver_summary: Paul Peret is the General Manager at RE/MAX Holdings (NYSE: RMAX), one of the world's largest real estate franchise networks with 140,000+ agents across 110+ countries, headquartered in Denver, Colorado. As General Manager, Paul operates at the intersection of corporate strategy and franchise field execution — accountable for outcomes across a distributed network of independently operated franchisees. He coordinates across technology, training, marketing, and regional broker development teams, while managing the growing competitive pressure from asset-light models like eXp Realty and technology-led brokerages like Compass. His core challenge is translating corporate strategic priorities into consistent, measurable execution across a franchise system that was built for a different competitive era — and doing so without adding proportional permanent headcount in a market-constrained environment.
outreach_goal: Book a 20-minute discovery conversation to explore whether Chris's Fractional COO model can help RE/MAX close the gap between corporate strategy and franchise field execution during a critical competitive inflection point
offer: Chris Ringenberg offers embedded Fractional COO and operational consulting engagements for franchise-heavy organizations at strategic inflection points. The model is not advisory — it is execution-focused operational leadership that sits inside the organization for the duration of a specific initiative. Engagements are scoped around defined outcomes: rebuilding franchise operations infrastructure, standardizing field execution across distributed networks, leading cross-functional transformation programs, or building the operational flywheel that makes a franchise system self-improving rather than dependent on constant corporate intervention. For organizations like RE/MAX navigating competitive disruption with shareholder cost scrutiny, the Fractional COO model delivers senior operational capability at variable cost — without a permanent hire.
asset_name: The Franchise Operations Maturity Model — a diagnostic framework for large franchise networks navigating competitive disruption
pain_points: The strategy-to-field execution gap is widening — corporate priorities are clear but the operational infrastructure to translate them into consistent franchisee-level outcomes has not kept pace with the scale and complexity of the network, The same franchise model that built 140000 agents is now creating rigidity — competing against asset-light and technology-first brokerages requires operational reinvention that the current infrastructure was not designed to deliver, The general manager role carries full accountability for outcomes across a distributed independent operator network without full authority — a structural tension that compounds when multiple transformation initiatives run simultaneously with finite internal resources
tone: Executive-level and consultative — peer-to-peer between two senior operational leaders, insight-first and direct, no generic compliments, no fluff, grounded in the specific competitive and operational reality of running a global franchise network in a disrupted market
